In the seventh month, Tian Yanyi of Gao and his son Chengbao and one hundred twenty others came to court; headcloths, robes, vessels, and gifts were bestowed, and Chengbao was made River-and-Mountain Envoy and Overall Supervisor of Pacification for the Nine Streams and Ten Caves.

田彥伊子承寶等百二十二人 means Yanyi's son Chengbao and others, 122 persons; Yanyi himself did not come, and the count is 122.
In year four Tian Chengxiiao and 372 other chiefs from An, Yuan, Shun, Nan, Yongning, and Zhuoshui presented tribute.
In year four Tian Chengxiao and 372 other chiefs from An, Yuan, Shun, Nan, Yongning, and Zhuoshui presented tribute.

In the fourth year, Tian Chengxiiao and three hundred seventy-two other Man chieftains of An, Yuan, Shun, Nan, Yongning, and Zhuoshui prefectures came to offer tribute.
In the fourth year, Tian Chengxiao and three hundred seventy-two other Man chieftains of An, Yuan, Shun, Nan, Yongning, and Zhuoshui prefectures came to offer tribute.

In year five the throne proclaimed: "Those stream-cave tribes who yesterday restored the Hankou captives and the fifty men they had taken shall receive special appointments and may continue to present tribute.

In year five the throne proclaimed: "Those stream-cave tribes who yesterday restored the Han captives and the fifty men they had taken shall receive special appointments and may continue to present tribute.
漢口 here means Han persons (captives), as elsewhere in this chapter, not the city Hankou.

In the fifth year, an edict stated: "Yesterday permission was granted to the stream-cave Man and Yi who returned those previously seized at Hankou and the fifty persons — they are specially granted official titles and still permitted to come with tribute.

In the fifth year, an edict stated: "Yesterday permission was granted to the stream-cave Man and Yi who returned the Han people previously seized and the fifty persons — they are specially granted official titles and still permitted to come with tribute.
漢口 here means Han persons (captives), as elsewhere in this chapter, not the city Hankou.

At the outset, the greatest chieftain of the Northern River Man was the Peng clan, which for generations held Xi Prefecture; the prefecture had three parts — Upper, Middle, and Lower Xi — and moreover six prefectures: Longci, Tianci, Zhongshun, Baojing, Ganhua, and Yongshun; and eleven prefectures: Yi, An, Yuan, Xin, Gei, Fu, Lai, Ning, Nan, Shun, and Gao — twenty in all, each with a prefect installed.

At the outset, the greatest chieftain of the Northern River Man was the Peng clan, which for generations held Xi Prefecture; the prefecture had three parts — Upper, Middle, and Lower Xi — and moreover six prefectures: Longci, Tianci, Zhongshun, Baojing, Ganhua, and Yongshun; and eleven prefectures: Yi, An, Yuan, Xin, Ji, Fu, Lai, Ning, Nan, Shun, and Gao — twenty in all, each with a prefect installed.
給州 is read Ji (as the idiomatic translation has it), not Gei.
In year three Rumeng killed Wenwan; Suo's ninety-two followers surrendered; Suo was restored as military commander, the rest given stipend posts.
In year three Rumeng killed Wenwan; his son Rusuo led ninety-two followers to surrender; Rusuo was made Overall Military Commander of Fu Prefecture, the rest given stipend posts.
儒索 is Rusuo (Ru- generation name, like Rumeng); 復州 is the place name Fu Prefecture, not "restore".

In the third year, Rumeng attacked and killed Wenwan; his son Suo led ninety-two followers to submit; Suo was appointed to restore the prefectural post of overall military commander, and the rest were given stipend offices.

In the third year, Rumeng attacked and killed Wenwan; his son Rusuo led ninety-two followers to submit; Rusuo was appointed Overall Military Commander of Fu Prefecture (Fuzhou), and the rest were given stipend offices.
儒索 is Rusuo (Ru- generation name, like Rumeng); 復州 is the place name Fu Prefecture, not "restore".
Zhang Dun oversaw both rivers; Li Ping won over Shiyan while Zhang Jingxu, Peng Deru, Xiang Yongsheng, Tan Wenmeng, and Tan Yanba surrendered their lands — and Shiyan yielded.
Zhang Dun oversaw both rivers; Li Ping won over Shiyan while Zhang Jingwei, Peng Deru, Xiang Yongsheng, Tan Wenmeng, and Tan Yanba surrendered their lands — and Shiyan yielded.
張景謂: 謂 is read wei, so the name is Zhang Jingwei.

Zhang Dun administered the Southern and Northern Rivers; Hubei Judicial Intendant Li Ping recruited Shiyan; Man of oath-subordinate prefectures Zhang Jingxu, Peng Deru, Xiang Yongsheng, Tan Wenmeng, and Tan Yanba each returned their lands to the registers, and Shiyan then submitted.

張景謂: 謂 is read wei, so the name is Zhang Jingwei.

Sentence lacked its opening and ran the reign title into Hubei; restores 元豐八年，湖北轉運司言.

Later Shu Guangxiu of Xia lost his people by extortion.

Thereafter there was Shu Guangxiu of Xia Prefecture, who because of exploiting his people excessively was not obeyed.
舒光秀 is surname Shu plus given name Guangxiu; the run-together form is an error.
An edict went to Hunan, northern Hunan, and Guangxi: "The empire holds all within the seas; its duty is to win over those far away.
An edict went to the Hunan, Hubei, and Guangxi circuits: "The empire holds all within the seas; its duty is to win over those far away.
湖南、北 abbreviates 湖南、湖北 (the Hunan and Hubei circuits).
An edict instructed Hunan, North Hunan, and the Guangxi circuit, saying: "The state maps and governs the four seas; its task lies in treating distant peoples gently.
An edict instructed the Hunan, Hubei, and Guangxi circuits, saying: "The state maps and governs the four seas; its task lies in treating distant peoples gently.
湖南、北 abbreviates 湖南、湖北 (the Hunan and Hubei circuits).

劉沆: 沆 is read hang; the name is Liu Hang.

Kang marched in force under the letter's authority; more than two thousand surrendered and were sent home, while leaders Deng Wenzhi, Huang Wensheng, and Huang Shiyuan were made third-class attendants.

Hang marched in force under the letter's authority; more than two thousand surrendered and were sent home, while leaders Deng Wenzhi, Huang Wensheng, and Huang Shiyuan were made third-class attendants.
